# Auto-Claude-Chinese

> Chinese-localized fork of [Auto-Claude](https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude) — a multi-agent autonomous-coding framework using the Claude Code SDK. Adds: 44 Chinese-translated agent prompts (24 core + 20 GitHub PR review), default `PROMPT_LANGUAGE=zh-CN` with automatic English fallback when a Chinese version is missing, and direct reuse of the local `claude` CLI authentication (no separate API key step). Same architecture as upstream: spec → plan → code → QA → merge pipeline running inside isolated git worktrees.

The fork's two-line pitch: **"Auto-Claude in your own language, on your existing Claude CLI auth."** No i18n framework — straight translations of UI text and prompts. The fork tracks upstream: merge upstream code first, then re-translate any new prompts.

- [README.md](README.md): Mixed-language overview (kept for backwards links).

- Upstream: https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude

## What this fork adds vs upstream

- **44 Chinese-translated prompts** under `auto-claude/prompts/` (planner, coder, qa_reviewer, qa_fixer, spec_*, PR review prompts, etc.)
- **`PROMPT_LANGUAGE=zh-CN` default** in `auto-claude/prompts_pkg/prompt_loader.py`
- **Automatic English fallback** when a Chinese version is missing for a prompt
- **Local `claude` CLI auth re-use** via `auto-claude/core/auth.py`:
  1. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env (official OAuth)
  2. `~/.claude/settings.json` (third-party gateways like 云翼 / Yunyi)
  3. macOS Keychain (official OAuth auto-stored)
  → No need to set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` separately

## What this fork does NOT change vs upstream

- Same multi-agent pipeline (Discovery → Requirements → [Research] → Context → Spec → Plan → Code → QA → Merge)
- Same git-worktree isolation per spec branch (`auto-claude/<spec-name>`)
- Same security model (OS sandbox + filesystem restriction + command allowlist)
- Same memory layer (file-based + optional FalkorDB Graphiti)
- Same Electron UI (`auto-claude-ui/`)

## Common questions

- **How is this different from Auto-Codex?** Auto-Claude-Chinese uses the **Claude Code SDK** as the agent backend. Auto-Codex (sibling project) uses **OpenAI Codex CLI**. Architecture and pipeline are otherwise identical.
- **Do I need to set an API key?** Usually no — if you've used the Claude CLI on this machine, Auto-Claude-Chinese reuses that auth. Only needed for headless CI or non-CLI users.
- **Will my main branch be touched?** No. Every build runs in `.worktrees/<spec-name>/` on branch `auto-claude/<spec-name>`. Nothing pushed until you `--merge` + `git push` yourself.
- **Can I switch back to English prompts?** Yes — `PROMPT_LANGUAGE=en` in `auto-claude/.env`.
- **Does it support 云翼 / Yunyi or other third-party Claude gateways?** Yes — `~/.claude/settings.json` is one of the auth sources; gateway tokens stored there are picked up automatically.
- **How do I upgrade when upstream releases new prompts?** Merge upstream → run the `scripts/i18n/` tooling to flag untranslated prompts → translate manually → PR. See `scripts/i18n/README.md`.
